</speech>

<speech by="#hon_member">

<from>*An <person refersTo="hansard_za">HON. MEMBER</person>:</from>

<p>What about Joe Stalin?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>You would not venture that even in Russia.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_finance">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF FINANCE</person>:</from>

<p>In no other country have regulations been enforced as mildly as in this country. I think the policy was right, but seeing that hon. members thought it was right in certain circumstances they must not now ask that we should apply them in the strictest manner where the law has not been &#x2018;transgressed. Their attitude is that we must proceed mildly against nazism but drastically against communism. That will not work. There is another point. The hon. member spoke about regulations and referred to lotteries. The same thing applies to lotteries. The <span class="col_8013-8014" refersTo="page_0308"/>hon. member knows that for years and years there have been raffles at church bazaars and other bazaars.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>When were you last at a church bazaars? It never happens at a church bazaar.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I have been at many church bazaars where raffles were run.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>These must have been Synagogue bazaars.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>These have never been prevented. In any case during the time of the Nationalist Party from 1924 to 1932 such raffles were actually run at church bazaars, all churches being concerned and no &#x2019; steps were taken against them. During the war the policy was indeed not to permit lotteries on the streets, except where money was being collected for war purposes and war charitable institutions. We did not intervene there unless it was clear that a profit was being made or a big commission was being paid out. Then we took immediate steps, and hon. members need merely look at the records of the courts to see how many prosecutions have been instituted in connection with that. Strong supervision was exercised in this connection by the police. Hon. members speak about Communism and what they describe as the communist danger. It appears that if anyone is a communist and he speaks, they want us to prosecute him. The communists form a political party who have a perfect right to exist so long as they act within the limits of the law. If they do not transgress the law there is no action we can take against them. It is obvious, however, that should the law be broken action will&#x2019; be taken. If the law is broken it does not matter whether it is the communists or any other party, but I have always said when allegations have been made against the communists: Point out to me where the law has been broken. Now we hear about speeches, communist speeches in connection with their cause. Well, I want to say that the communist speeches have not been nearly so strong as the speeches that have been made by certain hon. members of the Opposition in connection with the war. Incitement!</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strauss">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. R. STRAUSS</person>:</from>

<p>We let you have it, that is all.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>And if a communist wants to let you have it, in turn, you do not want to allow that.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>We did not run round amongst the natives and run you down amongst them</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I do not want to go into that, but the Nazis did in fact go round amongst the natives in the country and inflamed them a good deal.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>What has our Party got to do with that?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>And what have we to do with the communists?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strydom">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. G. STRYDOM</person>:</from>

<p>How many Nazis have been arrested for inciting the natives?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Many have been arrested.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strydom">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. G. STRYDOM</person>:</from>

<p>Why do you not arrest the communists who have done the same thing?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The communists are not doing it in a subversive way. The Nazis are doing it subversively, with subversive purposes, and hon. members know that as well as I do. The communists, as such, are a lawful party and the department can only be asked to take action where they infringe the law.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#louw">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">LOUW</person>:</from>

<p>You are shutting your eyes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Why do you not bring your charges so that they can be investigated? Why do you not mention instances?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strauss">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. R. STRAUSS</person>:</from>

<p>When we bring a complaint to you you say: &#x201C;Go and see Wyley.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The hon. member for Westdene spoke a great deal here about the Brakpan case. He knows very well that for a certain reason Mr. Rabie was dischaged from the Licensing Board. Until that time he served and he was messenger of the court. He was messenger of the court and he was appointed to the Liquor Licensing Board, and I regard that as very undesirable. Such a messenger is an official of the court.</p>

<p>He serves under a magistrate. He is dependent, because his engagement is on a monthly basis, and it is not desirable that such people should serve on a licensing board. The fact that this was the case before is no justification. I have laid down the policy that as far as the Department is concerned absolutely no messengers of the court may serve on licensing boards.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MENTZ</person>:</from>

<p>When was this policy laid down?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The minute I discovered that Rabie was a member of the Liquor Licensing Board.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strauss">

<from><span class="col_8015-8016" refersTo="page_0309"/>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. R. STRAUSS</person>:</from>

<p>It was a policy against Rabie.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Twenty years is as a minute in his eyes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>In other instances it was also laid down at the request of the other side of the House, although not in connection with the Liquor Licensing Board. It was brought to my notice that a messenger of the court was chairman of a branch of the United Party, and I took immediate steps that he should resign. Now there is the other case of Mitchell. I want to say here clearly that Mitchell was for a long period Mayor of Brakpan. He was a member of the Licensing Board. The question then came up whether he could sit as a member of the Licensing Board when an application by his brother was being dealt with. He sought information himself. He consulted a magistrate, and a magistrate advised him not to take the session. He then approached the Department of Justice, and the Under-Secretary also advised him that he ought not to attend the session but he did not say that he might not sit.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>Because he could not say that.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Exactly. He took his own opinion and sat. There was nothing secret about the matter. Everyone of them knew about it. He made a mistake there and the judge ticked him off strongly. But it was not done in secret, and in future he will not sit. But for a long time he was a member of the Licensing Board.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>What do you mean when you say he will not sit again?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Not if the case of his brother comes up. That is all that the court decided.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>The court said it was very improper for him to have sat.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I accept the decision of the court entirely. However, it was no secret, but really to make a test.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Come, come!</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The Department cannot say that he may not sit. In the future he will again be able to sit. His information was, and I believe he also took legal opinion, that he could sit. The judge stated quite explicitly that he sat not by way of a test but to try to further his brother&#x2019;s case.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>The judge stated very clearly that he sat not to test the matter but to try to advance his brother&#x2019;s case.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Well, apparently he did not advance his brother&#x2019;s case very much, because his brother lost., The case was widely discussed. Mr. Mitchell had a good record.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>You call that a good record?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>He was Mayor of Brakpan for a long time,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Was he recommended by the town council?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>He was always a member.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>After the court case?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No, that time he was not recommended. Then another political party got the upper hand. Then someone had to be appointed, and here was Mitchell who otherwise had a very good record.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>&#x201C;Otherwise.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>He was then re-appointed. He had long experience, and the point on which they differed was decided against him and the case will not arise again, but neither the Department nor anyone else told him that he could not sit. He went to the magistrate, and there was no secret about that.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MENTZ</person>:</from>

<p>You have only spoken about Rabie, who was not re-appointed. What about Vorster? Why did you refuse to accept a recommendation to appoint him?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I am free to exercise my discretion, and after going into the matter I regarded that as undesirable.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Do you regard the judgment of the court as a reflection on Mr. Mitchell&#x2019;s bona fides?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Not on his bona fides.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Did you hear what the judge said?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>It was a reflection upon his action. He made no secret of the fact that he was going to sit. I accept that as being the case. Hon. members on the other side cannot complain that I did not accept the recommendation of the Town Council of Brakpan. During the years when the Nationalist Party was in power and when the South African Party had a majority on the Town Council <span class="col_8017-8018" refersTo="page_0310"/>of Brakpan, Brakpan made a recommendation then that was not accepted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Was it in connection with a man with a record such as this?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Was the man condemned by the judge?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>He was not condemned by the judge. He acted wrongly in this case, but if he had not sat he would not have been condemned.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Of course not.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The charge against him was this, that seeing his brother was an applicant he should have recused himself in connection with the application. That was the point. The reflection upon him was only that he sat in this specific instance.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Do you know that the judge said: &#x201C;The only honourable way would have been &#x2026;.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I know the judge expressed himself strongly and condemned him for having sat.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>In other words, it was a dishonourable thing for him to have sat.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>That is what the judge said, but he did not do it mala fides; he did it openly and everyone knew about it and otherwise he had a very good record and had always been recommended.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>The judge said: &#x201C;Mitchell has a mind which cannot see that the honourable way &#x2026;.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I admit he expressed himself strongly.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>If I commit a theft in such a case am I a thief?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>There was no theft committed. He did not commit any offence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>But it was a dishonourable thing.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>He did it under a misunderstanding.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>No.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>He was advised and thought he could still sit. If the United Party had obtained a majority at Brakpan they would again have appointed him.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>That would have been a reflection on the Saps of Brakpan. No wonder the United Party did not get a majority.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>It is an ugly reflection on the United Party.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I want to go further. In connection with this matter judgment was given on the 25th January the year before last, and he continued to sit for a whole year, and neither the Nationalists of Brakpan nor the members of the United Party, nor the Brakpan municipality on whose behalf he was appointed, nor anyone else had any objection.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>You must know that they could not do that.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No one took exception to him sitting. No one said that he should be taken off. Not once were representations made against his re-appointment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>But they only sit once a year. How could they have raised an objection earlier?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>It was only after he was appointed when he could no longer be removed that an objection was made. Not the slightest censure was passed on him in the town council. That could have been done. There was not the slightest objection by any member of the Nationalist Party at Brakpan. But after he was re-appointed &#x2026;.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>How could they have objected; under what Act?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Very easily. What prevented them from asking him to resign? What prevented them from passing a vote of censure?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#hon_member">

<from>*An <person refersTo="hansard_za">HON. MEMBER</person>:</from>

<p>Do not be so stupid.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Why were no steps taken? They could easily have introduced a motion of censure in the Brakpan Town Council and asked that he should resign. But nothing was done until he was appointed. The first time that I heard that anyone at Brakpan was raising an objection was after he had been re-appointed. They all knew that new appointments had to be made and they did not stir a finger to say that the department should not appoint him again.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Did the town council recommend him?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from><span class="col_8019-8020" refersTo="page_0311"/>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MENTZ</person>:</from>

<p>Was it only Nationalists of the town council who registered a protest?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No objection was made before he was re-appointed.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MENTZ</person>:</from>

<p>Please answer my question. In reference to the deputation that called on you did these protests come only from the Nationalists of the town council, or were the protests also on behalf of the public?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>They were not all Nationalists. They spoke on behalf of others.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>I said that this was an insult to the Saps at Brakpan. I thought they knew better.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>When hon. members talk about this matter I should like them to tell me why no objection was raised in the town council, why no motion of censure was proposed? But it was after his re-appointment and after Rabie was discharged that it was first brought up. The hon. member for Graaff-Reinet (Mr. G. P. Steyn) also mentioned the question of the Germans as did the hon. member for Wakkerstoom (Mr. J. G. W. van Niekerk). Weichardt&#x2019;s case is still sub judice, and I consequently cannot deal with it here. In regard to the Germans, the war is over, the fighting is finished, but no one knows yet what the position is going to be. The war against Japan is still in progress and provisionally the present procedure will be followed.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>I spoke about the theft by the district surgeon.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>As far as that matter is concerned it has never been brought to my notice. I have asked for information, and I will go into it. At the moment I do not know anything about it.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>Will it be referred to the Medical Council?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I shall first have to investigate the matter.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Will you carry out the law?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Yes, that is always done in my Department.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sauer">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SAUER</person>:</from>

<p>Will you not make another emergency regulation?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I think I have now dealt with all the points and that hon. members will agree with me.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>I want to turn to another point, but I promise the Minister we shall come back to his answer. I should like him to have time, however, to reflect on the matter I shall bring up because it is a matter of great importance to the sound administration of justice in our country. I refer to the application of War Measure 57 of 1941. That war measure has placed a special power in the hands of the Minister of Justice, and that is the power in certain circumstances to take any person into custody and to question him, to lock him up and keep him locked up until he answers questions to the satisfaction of the Minister of Justice. That is a very exceptional power that has been given to the Minister. It is a power that is unknown in ordinary circumstances. It is a power the granting of which can only be justified by war conditions. It should only be applied and strictly applied, in conformity with the terms of the regulation itself. I shall now tell the House briefly what powers it gives. In the first place it is restricted to people who are guilty or suspected of being guilty of a specified offence. That is the first qualification. Only three offences are mentioned, and these are acts of violence towards persons, damage to property, and theft. It is restricted to these three cases only, but ordinary cases do not fall under it. In addition to those another element is required, and that is that one of the three offences must have been committed with the intention of hampering the Government&#x2019;s war effort. That is what is essential. In the circumstances the Minister can place in custody a person whom he suspects of taking part in any of the offences concerned. It must be with the intention of hampering the war effort. Remember the words &#x201C;offence concerned&#x201D;. Consequently he can detain anyone he considers as taking part in that; and in the second place any person who is in possession of information in reference to the &#x201C;aforesaid offence&#x201D;. You see in each case it is nicely ringed in with the provision that it must be something in connection with an offence that is here described. He can question a person he has taken into custody in these circumstances, but here again only in reference to the offence mentioned, and nothing else than the offence mentioned&#x2014; and he can detain him further at any place he thinks suitable until the Minister is convinced&#x2014;the discretion rests with the Minister&#x2014;that that person has answered fully and truthfully all questions that have been put to him in connection with the offence mentioned. This is a very extra-ordinary power that is given to the Minister of Justice. One would have expected that that power could only be exercised strictly in terms of the proclamation, and that the Minister would have been at great pains to see that that measure was not applied in circumstances described in the proclamation itself. But my complaint now against the <span class="col_8021-8022" refersTo="page_0312"/>Minister is that he is applying this proclamation to cases that are not covered by the language of this war measure. That is my first complaint; and in the second place where he applies this, whether it is rightly done or not, the treatment he then accords people who taken into custody in terms of this regulation is of such a character that, to say the least&#x2014;you know that I am not prone to exaggerate&#x2014;it is a shock to any person&#x2019;s sense of justice. Here we have the exceptional case. I want to say in the first place, and I have already mentioned it here on the occasion of a motion that was proposed by the hon. member for Woodstock (Mr. Russell), that this measure is used in respect of cases that it was never intended to cover, and it is not only a single case that I am referring to; there are many cases of this sort, cases of infraction of the diamond laws, not cases of personal violence, not cases of damage to property and not cases of theft; and in every case there has been no suggestion that that particular offence was committed with the intention of hampering the Government in its war effort. In a number of cases it has been applied outside the scope of this section. I think the Minister will not deny that he has used this measure to bring to justice people he suspected of transgressing the diamond laws. Now I want to ask the Minister: Where does he get the right under this war measure to take people into custody in those circumstances and to hold them for examination when it is not one of these offences that is involved? But now I want to go further into a particular case, the case of Mr. Botes that was recently heard at Upington. He pleaded guilty and on that he was sentenced. I want to present his case to the House from these two standpoints. In the first place there was no question that it was one of those offences. There was no suggestion that it was the intention to hamper the Government&#x2019;s war effort, so in any event this war measure absolutely did not apply. But suppose for a moment that his case did fall under this, then I want to read out the sworn evidence that was given in the circuit court in the presence of a representative of the Attorney-General together with a challenge to the Crown to contest the facts mentioned there, a challenge that was not accepted. I may say that I have done everything in my power to check the facts that I have today submitted to the House and see they are absolutely correct, and that there is no question of exaggeration. Here is the evidence that was led. After that evidence was given by Mr. Botes he was cross examined by the representative of the Crown and during the cross-examination no doubt was thrown on the facts that he gave in his evidence. Now I should like to read the evidence out to you and then you can judge for yourselves. I only wish to add that the person was held for examination in connection with information which he was supposed to have in his possession in connection with a Mr. Kallie Kahn and Barney Diamond and Jack Feinman. I only want to add as a background to the picture that those people were all before the court and the statement that was eventually obtained from Mr. Botes had so little reference to their case that he was not even called on by the Crown as a witness. Consequently he was detained because he was in the possession of information, and yet the information they elicited from him was of such a character that the Crown did not consider it worth while calling him as a witness at the trial of these people. This evidence was led not only in the presence of the representative of the Attorney-General but also in the presence of the official who was in charge of this whole investigation with reference to diamond offences in the North-West. My time is nearly finished and I would rather read this evidence as a whole. [Time limit.]</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#shearer">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">V. L. SHEARER</person>:</from>

<p>There is just one point I would like to raise with the Minister and it arises as a result of a statement that the Minister issued recently wherein he requested the municipality of Durban to extend its present Civilian Protective Services in regard to the Civilian Guard to the end of October. I would like at this stage, firstly to associate myself with the remarks of the hon. Minister with regard to the praises he extended to this particular service in Durban which was conducted during this war, not for the sake of looking after the safety of Durban but in the national interest of the country. And, Sir, in undertaking that service in the national interest, the municipality of Durban have been put to considerable financial expenditure as a result of which there have always been negotiation between the Government on the one hand and the municipality on the other hand. The Minister did indicate in that statement that agreement had been reached in regard to a subsidy until the end of June. I would like the Minister to indicate, in view of the fact that he has asked that this service should be extended to the end of October, to what extent the Government is prepared to assist the municipality of Durban. I hope that in view of the trouble that existed in the past, in arriving at an agreement, and in view of the fact that we have been unable to come to an agreement in the matter, and as it would appear that agreement has been reached in so far as the extension of the service is concerned, the Minister will indicate to what extent the Government is prepared to extend further assistance to the municipality of Durban.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from><span class="col_8023-8024" refersTo="page_0313"/>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>I will now read the evidence to which I referred, in the case of the Crown versus Nicolaas Botes. The advocate put this question to Mr. Botes&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">I want you to tell us how you were arrested?&#x2014;On the morning of the 29th August, 1944, when I was still in bed, Capt. Rademeyer and Capt. Moss of the Police knocked at my door and asked me to get up as they wanted to see me.</block>

<p>Then he said what it was in connection with namely the cases of Kahn, Diamond and Feinman. The evidence reads further&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">You refused to make a statement?&#x2014;I said I knew nothing about it.</block>

<p>You were then in the charge office and said that you did not have the information? &#x2014;Yes, then Rademeyer said they were going to take me to Kimberley and they would detain me until I spoke&#x2014;they would keep me in custody until six months after peace had been signed.</p>

<p>They took you to Kimberley?&#x2014;The same time.</p>

<p>Did they allow you to see your wife?&#x2014;No, my wife was not at all well; she was under doctor&#x2019;s treatment and she had to undergo an operation. I requested permission to visit them but he would not allow me to.</p>

<p>How did you get your clothes?&#x2014;Police were sent to fetch them.</p>

<p>Were you given the opportunity of making any financial provision for your family? &#x2014;No, I requested permission to go to the bank to inform the manager to give my wife money if she needed it, but Rademeyer said I could not see anybody.</p>

<p>Were you taken to Kimberley that evening?&#x2014;That day we went through and at 6 p.m. we arrived there. On arrival they took everything away from me and locked me up in a cell.</p>

<p>Remember this is someone who was not condemned. This is a person who was detained for interrogation but he received the treatment meted out to a condemned prisoner.</p>

<p>Did they also take your cigarettes away? &#x2014;Everything. I had my clothes and sleeping kit and a handkerchief and except for them I had nothing.</p>

<p>Were you allowed a shaving set?&#x2014;No.</p>

<p>How long were you in that cell?&#x2014;I arrived there on Saturday at 6 p.m. and 14 days after that I was released.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#hon_members">

<from><person refersTo="hansard_za">*HON. MEMBERS</person>:</from>

<p>Disgraceful!</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>The advocate put the further question&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">Has a charge been brought against you at any time?&#x2014;No, I think the first charge was in November of last year.</block>

<p>In August he was taken into custody, as hon. members will remember.</p>

<p>Except for the police, did you ever see other people in the cell?&#x2014;No, except for the police I saw no private people; I requested to see a lawyer and was told that it was not permitted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#erasmus">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. C. ERASMUS</person>:</from>

<p>It sounds like Russia.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>It goes on&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">Are you a man who is healthy?&#x2014;Yes, to a certain extent I suffer from high blood pressure and insomnia, from the days of my childhood I have had a little trouble with my heart, but I am not an invalid.</block>

<p>Did you tell the police that you were a man who suffered from high blood pressure? &#x2014;I asked them whether they would give me a special cushion. I offered to pay anything for it. According to the specialist my head is very sensitive and I find it very difficult to lie comfortably without a special cushion.</p>

<p>You were prepared to pay for the cushion?&#x2014;Yes, any amount.</p>

<p>Did you have money?&#x2014;Yes, a few pounds.</p>

<p>You were in the cell for 14 days, were you given a bed?&#x2014;No, I slept on the floor.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#hon_members">

<from><person refersTo="hansard_za">*HON. MEMBERS</person>:</from>

<p>Disgraceful!</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>The question was put to him&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">What kind of floor was it?&#x2014;Cement.</block>

<p>What month was it?&#x2014;It was the 18th August in Kimberley.</p>

<p>Was it cold?&#x2014;It was abnormally cold.</p>

<p>Did you have any conveniences apart from the blankets on which you had to sleep?&#x2014;Absolutely nothing else.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MENTZ</person>:</from>

<p>It sounds like Siberia.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>The following question is&#x2014;</p>

<p><span class="col_8025-8026" refersTo="page_0314"/>You asked for a cushion and this was refused?&#x2014;Definitely.</p>

<p>You say it was very cold; were you allowed to sleep undisturbed at night?&#x2014; No, not during the night.</p>

<p>Why not?&#x2014;During the night at intervals of an hour or less one or two policemen came in and switched on the lights and looked round the cell and then went out again and slammed the door making a terrible noise, and then as I was about to go to sleep again, they came in again and so it went on right through the night.</p>

<p>Did this keep on for 14 days?&#x2014;Yes.</p>

<p>Could you sleep in the night?&#x2014;I suffer from insomnia and I could not sleep.</p>

<p>In those 14 days were you ever taken out for exercise or for a walk?&#x2014;The only exercise I had was on the 12th day I was there.</p>

<p>What happened then?&#x2014;I then asked Detective Grobbelaar to allow me to walk when he came to fetch me to go to the detective&#x2019;s office and this request was granted, and I walked to the detective&#x2019;s office.</p>

<p>Were you taken now and again to the detective&#x2019;s office?&#x2014;A few times, but always by motor.</p>

<p>When you arrived there did they interrogate you?&#x2014;Yes, they asked me to make a statement and when I did not I was taken back to the cell.</p>

<p>Were you given any reading matter while you were in the cell?&#x2014;I asked repeatedly for something to read. I said they could take my, food away and give me something to read.</p>

<p>Were you given something to read?&#x2014;I hope I am not letting out secrets, but through other channels I managed to get a Bible and a &#x201C;Kerkbode&#x201D;.</p>

<p>This was smuggled to you by one of the police?&#x2014;Yes.</p>

<p>Did you ask for something to read?&#x2014; I repeatedly asked them to give me something to pass the time.</p>

<p>As regards food, did you ask for food from an hotel and offer to pay for it?&#x2014; Yes, I did so.</p>

<p>What sort of food did they give you?&#x2014; In the morning one spoonful of porridge.</p>

<p>With milk and sugar?&#x2014;Just a little milk and sugar. In the morning I did not get early morning coffee and then with the porridge I got coffee. For lunch, about three slices of ordinary brown bread with half a cup of tea, and in the evening the same again as at lunch-time, that is to say two or three slices of ordinary bread and half a cup of tea. I may not eat the ordinary bread and I cannot drink tea. I repeatedly told them that I could not eat the bread and was also not allowed to drink tea.</p>

<p>You were forbidden under doctor&#x2019;s orders to drink tea or eat the ordinary bread?&#x2014;Yes, I have stomach trouble.</p>

<p>Was there ever a change in the meals? &#x2014;On Sunday we got a little meat; I measured it and it was about the size of my thumb.</p>

<p>Anything else?&#x2014;Then a small helping of vegetables, to this day I don&#x2019;t know what they were. That was on Sunday. Then on the following Thursday two eggs were sent in with the two slices of bread, but there was another fellow in another cell and he was sick.</p>

<p>He then said that he sent the eggs to the man who was sick&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">What about your health; on the 14th day you signed something, what sort of health were you in then?&#x2014;I had lost weight and was not feeling well, as anyone can understand, but I was not sick.</block>

<p>Did you find it easy to walk?&#x2014;Grobbelaar can vouch for this, I swayed in the street.</p>

<p>Did he have to help you?&#x2014;Practically.</p>

<p>On the 14th day you made a statement, why?&#x2014;It was the only way of being released from imprisonment and going home.</p>

<p>The police went to see you at Upington; have they now made provision for you? <i>&#x2014;I</i> asked Grobbelaar what the position was and to come to the house, and he said: &#x201C;We release people and they must make their own provision.&#x201D;</p>

<p>And then just this bit&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">What was the treatment meted out to you by various police officials?&#x2014;I am glad Mr. Beyers has asked me that. Apart from the cell they treated me with the greatest courtesy; for that all honour is due to them.</block>

<p>Thus here you have officials who apparently did everything in their power to be helpful; <span class="col_8027-8028" refersTo="page_0315"/>but in all probability there must be instructions issued. People who want to be friendly cannot at the same time act as inhumanly as this man was treated. I assert that a man who is detained under those circumstances, even though it is a case where the Minister is justified in detaining him for interrogation, cannot be otherwise treated than as an ordinary uncondemned prisoner, in other words, just as a person who is not yet condemned. Now I just want to refer the Minister to his own regulations. What is the treatment afforded to a person who is arrested for a crime, who is detained pending his trial? He has not yet been examined, and it is one of the basic principles of our criminal law that a person is deemed innocent until such time as his guilt has been proved. What is the treatment to be meted out to him? In the first place I will refer to the Act itself. Article 17 reads&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">Prisoners detained under an order, writ, or judgment of any court, made or given in civil proceedings, unconvicted prisoners awaiting trial for alleged offence &#x2026;. shall be allowed to procure for themselves from outside the gaol and to receive at proper hours therein such food, bedding, clothing, or other articles as may be approved by the Director, subject to a strict examination thereof and under such limitations and restrictions as may be prescribed by regulation.</block>

<p>Therefore when a person who is arrested for committing a crime, he is entitled, until such time as he is condemned, to demand to be able to get food and bedding from outside, and it was refused this person who was not even arrested as a result of his having committed a crime. [Time limit.]</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>&#x2020;*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>I want to revert to the story of the man who took the wrong turning, as the judge says here. He calls him: &#x201C;The first citizen of Brakpan who took the wrong turning&#x201D;. I should not have gone into this were it not for the astonishing answer given by the Minister today in connection with this matter. The Minister said very clearly here that this is a political matter. He clearly signified that if the United Party had been in the majority in Brakpan, in the town council, they would have re-appointed the man. He said that the Nationalist Party have acted similarly in the past, in other words, he is now turning it into a political matter. I have no strong objection to the fact that he should appoint a Party supporter, but my question to him is why he should appoint a person like this, &#x201C;the first citizen of Brakpan who took the wrong turning&#x201D;? He says here: &#x201C;Otherwise Mr. Mitchell has a very good record&#x201D;. But it is precisely in this matter, where he is appointed, that he has a bad and black record. I am once more obliged to read a few extracts from the court case. For the rest of the sitting of the board, he was suspended by the court. I will read further from the Judge&#x2019;s remarks&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">Why did it fail? What private interest or scheme had got such possession of Mitchell&#x2019;s mind that he could not see the only honourable way?</block>

<p>In other words he acted improperly&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">He acted dishonourably.</block>

<p>The Judge says&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">The path of integrity could scarcely have been more plainly indicated than it was by the magistrate and the UnderSecretary and yet the first citizen of Brakpan took the wrong turning.</block>

<p>Thus in this respect he did not follow &#x201C;the path of integrity&#x201D;, but on the contrary a dishonourable path. Then the Judge says&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">Were if necessary for my decision I should not hesitate to hold that actual bias has been proved.</block>

<p>In other words, the Judge declares here that Mr. Mitchell was prejudiced in his decision. In other words, he was not unbiased. To wit he proved that he was biased. Then the Judge says further&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">If a case so scandalous succeeded in passing the scrutiny of the court, the standards hitherto applied in judging of such matters, would have to be revised, and the principles of natural justice modified.</block>

<p>We must remember that the word &#x201C;scandalous&#x201D; is a serious term for a Judge to use. I believe that there are members on the other side of the House&#x2014;I do not know how many&#x2014;but I believe that there are members on the other side who still have some feeling for right and justice and for efficient administration in the country.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#werth">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">WERTH</person>:</from>

<p>For clean government</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>&#x2020;*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Now I want to say this. Say for example that the man who was ejected was a Nationalist and we raised objection thereto. How would the Minister not have quoted from this finding to us, and then he would have said to us: &#x201C;You want me to appoint the man whom the Judge described as &#x2018;dishonourable&#x2019;&#x201D;? But today he pushes it aside. What I want to know is this: Who put pressure to bear on him; who recommended to him that Mitchell should be re-appointed? He is now hiding behind the Town Council of Brakpan; <span class="col_8029-8030" refersTo="page_0316"/>yes, they have not moved a finger to prevent Mitchell from being appointed. I take it that the town council members of Brakpan are honourable men who did not expect the Minister to do such a dishonourable thing and to appoint the man who shortly before was branded by the Judge as somebody who behaved &#x201C;dishonourably&#x201D;.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MENTZ</person>:</from>

<p>But the public held meetings of protest.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>&#x2020;*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Can anyone possessing a feeling of decency imagine that the Minister would come and eject a man who has a clean record and then appoint Mr. Mitchell? The Minister says that otherwise he has a clean record, but he puts out a man whose record is unblemished and he appoints a man who does not possess a clean record. I say that there is somthing behind this matter, the cause of which we would like to know. We are not satisfied. I appeal to hon. members on the other side who also have a feeling of decency, to tell me whether they think it is right that the Minister should go ahead and act in this way. Can there be any confidence in the liquor licensing boards which are appointed by the Minister if such things happen? What guarantee has he that tomorrow there will not again be an unworthy deed committed by the same man? No, the hon. Minister&#x2019;s defence is very werk. He is completely at sea and says that because Mitchell has a good record otherwise, he will appoint him again. He is appointing him on a case in connection with which he has a dishonourable record. There are just a few other things which the Minister has not replied to, and I insist on the Minister&#x2019;s informing us what the position is. His Government will never tell us what they are going to do with people who furnished false information during the war to the Government, those cases where it has been proved to their own satisfaction that false information was given. The Minister refuses to say anything about that. We still want to know whether they are simply going to allow those people to walk about freely and say to them: &#x201C;You gave us false information; you have received your reward; proof has now been furnished that that evidence was false, but you can go&#x201D;. I would like to know what the Minister intends doing. Hon. members in the House spoke about our viewpoint in connection with acts of violence. I thought the objection against the Hon. Leader of the Opposition was always that he warned against acts of violence and gangsterdom. He uttered an early warning. We on this side, both in this House and outside and in our newspapers, warned time and time again against acts of violence. We urged our supporters to have nothing to do with acts of violence. Now hon. members come along and ask us whether we still protest against acts of violence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#malan">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">MALAN</person>:</from>

<p>They attacked me for that.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>&#x2020;*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Yes, they said here that the Hon. Leader of the Opposition first of all supported the Ossewa-Brandwag and now he is accusing them of gangsterdom. Time and again the Leader of the Opposition issued a warning against acts of violence and gangsterdom and we did so as well. The Minister of Justice accuses us today of having delivered vicious speeches in this period and of having incited people against the Government.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#bekker">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. J. BEKKER</person>:</from>

<p>Quite right.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>&#x2020;*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Can the Minister not draw a line between a political opponent who attacks his Government and people who on the sly have incited the kaffirs and the coloureds against the white man, against the Government and the country? Does he not differentiate between the two? Can he not see a difference between his political opponent who openly expresses his opinion of the Government on public platforms and the man who quietly and slyly goes and incites the non-European population and antagonises them against the European population? Does he not see any difference in that? They have done nothing to prevent those dangerous happenings taking place. The Minister&#x2019;s own leader, the present Prime Minister, issued a warning as early as 1929 and he said&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">I hope that the Government will ensure that this movement (namely the communistic movement), is watched and that these matters are not allowed to develop until perhaps one day a spirit will originate among the natives which it will be difficult to quell.</block>

<p>Those were the present Prime Minister&#x2019;s words in 1929. He said&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">It will be the darkest day for this country, both for Europeans and natives, if we cannot uphold law and order. The natives of this country ought to know that they receive just and fair treatment from the Europeans, but they also ought to know that obedience to the law is expected of them &#x2026;.</block>

<p>[Time limit.]</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>When I spoke last I said that the position of the people detained by the department for questioning could be more or less compared with the position of people who in the ordinary course of the adminis <span class="col_8031-8032" refersTo="page_0317"/>tration of justice are detained for trial or as witnesses. The law prescribes that people so detained are entitled to food and clothing and to visits from their legal advisers from outside. The prison regulations provide for that, and I would like to mention a few of those regulations. We find, for example, that Regulation No. 605 provides that such a person&#x2019;s legal adviser may visit him, something that was refused in the case of Botes. Regulation 608 provides for bedding, which was also refused in the case of Botes. Regulation 609 says that none of the person&#x2019;s property may be taken away except dangerous weapons or articles that may be used to facilitate his escape. No. 612 provides that he may smoke; but this was denied Botes. No. 613 lays down that reading matter may be received by him, but this too was denied Botes. In every respect we find that the man detained for examination in this case did not even get the treatment that a criminal would get when awaiting trial. This is the least that such a person may expect, and I should like to know under what authority the Minister acted in dealing with these people in this way, because it does not redound to the credit of his department even if they did this to a prisoner who had already been convicted. It is a very serious matter, and there was an occasion when the Appeal Court had reason to express itself on the treatment of persons detained for trial, because such treatment as was meted out to them corresponded to a certain extent with the treatment Botes received. I refer to the case of Whitaker versus Roos and Bateman heard by the Appeal Court in 1912. This man&#x2019;s complaint was that before conviction he was not permitted (1) to take any exercise except two hours a day. In the case of Botes he had one hour&#x2019;s exercise for the first time after 12 days; (2) that they were not allowed to smoke for 12 days; (3) that they were not allowed to receive newspapers; (4) that they were refused an interview with their legal advisers. I have already shown this also happened in this case. (5) That other articles besides those that are prohibited were taken from them. Then (6) the person complained that &#x201C;he was tormented by the sound of corporal punishment&#x201D; that was given to other offenders. In the same way in this case it was complained that the person could not get any rest at night because every hour people were coming in so that he was not allowed to rest. What did the judge say in that case I have referred to? I want to say that this is not a matter that affects this side of the House or that side of the House. It is a matter that affects the citizens of the country because it affects our administration of justice, which we have always regarded with pride and we are exceptionally jealous that nothing should be done to endanger its foundations. In his judgment Lord De Villiers said&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">The harshness would become absolutely intolerable if directors of prisons or governors of gaols had it within their power to add to the misfortune of imprisonment the disgrace and torture of confinement in a small punishment cell of 4 ft. by 9 ft., without sufficient light, with no bed to sleep upon, with insufficient means of&#x2019; exercise, without books to read, without the companionship of a single soul and without even the consolation afforded by a smoke.</block>

<p>In this case we are concerned with a person who was detained and who after 14 days made a statement in which he admitted his guilt. I do not want to say anything here about the offence he committed. This opinion of the judge&#x2019;s has also no relation to the nature of the crime. It has to do with the question of the treatment of a person before he has been convicted of the offence. I should also like to refer to a remark by Sir James Rose-Innes in regard to people who were concerned in sabotage. Inter alia, he said&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">I would remark that, however reprehensible a man&#x2019;s views may be, he is entitled to have his personal liberty adequately protected.</block>

<p>The person may be a criminal or someone who wanted to use dynamite against his fellowmen, but that has nothing to do with the requirement that a man&#x2019;s personal rights may not be impinged on before judgment actually is given. Lord De Villiers stated further&#x2014;</p>

<block name="quote">By all means let the authorities use all their efforts to put criminals and suspected criminals under lock and key, but when once they have done this let them remember that punishment should only begin when the guilt of the prisoners has been established by judgment of a court of law.</block>

<p>I assert that the methods employed in the case of Botes closely approximate the third degree and the methods of the Gestapo and the Ogpu, which are unknown in a civilised country like South Africa. I have presented the facts and the Minister of Justice is unable to state that those facts are not correct. I have checked the facts as far as possible, and I say that so far as I cap check them they are correct. These things must have occurred in pursuance of instructions, because the officials themselves were sympathetic, and I say that this reveals a state of affairs that we may not tolerate in our country. If these facts are in any way true then it is a matter that must <span class="col_8033-8034" refersTo="page_0318"/>be immediately rectified. We have always had confidence in our administration of justice in this country, and one of the foundations of our administration of justice is that a person must be regarded as innocent until his guilt has been established by a court. He may not be punished before he has been convicted. A definite encroachment has been made here of what must be regarded as a sacred and inviolable principle of our administration of justice. I have stated I appeal to hon. members on the other side who have any sense of justice still, that they should not allow the foundations of our administration of justice to be tampered with. Their sense of justice must surely have received a shock by these revelations, and they will agree with me that we dare not allow conduct of this nature to occur in our country, and that there should be immediate restitution in respect of the injustice that was done, and also that those persons should be punished who were responsible for the instructions that people held for questioning should be treated in this way. This is certainly not the first instance. This is the instance that I checked, but my information is that there are other cases besides this. Now I should like to know from the Minister what his policy is. If this is the way he is going to apply this regulation and this principle then I maintain that it is high time that War Measure No. 57 should immediately be repealed.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I wish just briefly to repeat what I said a little while ago. I want to deal with this matter on its merits and not from a Party viewpoint. Hon. members on the other side have the right to make as much propaganda with it as they wish. My duty is to deal with the matter objectively here. We have here to deal with a case that is known to all the people in that neighbourhood. It was known to everyone in that neighbourhood that this person who was a member of the Licensing Board proposed his brother&#x2019;s application. This individual also did not immediately attend the session. In the first instance he asked the opinion of the magistrate, who did not tell him that he might not sit, though he advised him not to. Then he consulted the Secretary for Justice.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>And they all told him not to sit.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>They did not tell him that he might not sit. They told him it was a question of whether it was advisable whether he should sit, and from that angle they advised him not to sit. He also took other advice to the effect that he was appointed, and that he was perfectly entitled to take his seat. Everyone knew that the case would be a test case.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Can you tell us who gave that advice?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I do not know that, but that is his affair.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Why did he not submit a sworn declaration to the court?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I do not know. I only know that he took advice and he must then have thought he was entitled to sit. If he did not think that he would not have attended a session, because then he would have known that he would have spoilt the whole case. He made a mistake. But everyone knew that the matter would go to the court. The Judge strongly criticised his action.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strydom">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. G. STRYDOM</person>:</from>

<p>He said it was disgraceful.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I must accept what the Judge said. He gave his finding on this one point. The Judge only suspended him on this one point, as far as his having sat is concerned, but he did not do more. He did not condemn his action in connection with any other matter. The Judge only said that he acted wrongly in connection with having sat on that one occasion.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>But the court could do nothing more, and the Judge said that in that case the man had acted disgracefully.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Yes, on that point he was punished. The Judge made no further suggestion that the man ought to resign or that he was not competent to sit. If the Judge would have done that then he would not have Said that a person should only be suspended in that one case.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>But the Judge could not do that because only that one case was before him.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Although it would have been much better if he had not sat he did so openly and honourably and why should we go beyond the punishment that the Judge imposed on him?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>But there was no further application.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The Judge suspended him and left it at that. He made no further observations. Everyone knew that this person was appointed for a year and the Judge passed no reflection at all on the rest of his conduct. Nor did the town council at that time make any objection to it. The first time they made <span class="col_8035-8036" refersTo="page_0319"/>an objection was in December when he was re-appointed. He had been punished in connection with the one case, but there was no suggestion that he should not attend any further sitting, or that he could not again be appointed. The further facts of the case are that this man had done public service for a long time and had behaved well. On this one point his judgment was wrong; but he did it openly, and why should we now continue to punish him? I think this is a complete answer to this case that members on the other side have mentioned.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#strydom">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. G. STRYDOM</person>:</from>

<p>But if a man has such a weak judgment that it is possible for him to make such a blunder, it must be obvious that he is not fit to serve on such a board.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>But even a magistrate cannot say that he might not do that. He acted in the open and he made a mistake as far as his judgment was concerned. For that he was rebuked and punished, and it is not for us to punish him further. It was not a question that was clear and there was no previous decision. After that finding there was not the slightest objection made against him from any quarter to his continuing to serve on the Licensing Board. No one asked him to resign. It was only when he was re-appointed they made an objection.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#steyn">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">G. P. STEYN</person>:</from>

<p>They did not recommend him again.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No, the town council did not recommend him. He was re-appointed, and that is the whole explanation and the reply as far as that case is concerned. I may not have convinced members opposite, but I myself am absolutely convinced about the position. Now I want to come to the point that has been broached by the hon. member for Fauresmith (Dr. D&#x00F6;nges). I shall not discuss the facts and I shall only deal with the matter generally. As far as the general principles of justice are concerned, I agree with him. I have not the facts before me, and therefore I do not want to go exactly into the merits of the case nor to go into those facts. I shall go into the facts later, because I have never had them before me. I wish to confine myself more particularly to the general principle. Let me admit at once that no one likes that sort of regulation, and that sort of measure. No one wants them in normal times, and it was only the state of emergency in the country that brought us to the stage of instituting those regulations. The police have acted absolutely well in terms of the regulations. The hon. member is now pointing out that those regulations are very rigorous, but he loses sight of the circumstances under which they were enforced. He is judging them from the angle of ordinary circumstances of the country, and that is absolutely wrong. He must remember that the country was passing through a period of war, and in a period of war we have to deal with martial law. He therefore should not compare those regulations with the normal regulations in peace time but he should compare them with the regulations we would have under martial law, and which other countries apply under martial law.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Where it is stated in Regulation 57 that power has been granted to treat people in this way when they are detained?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The regulation is perfectly clear that such a person can be detained as we have done.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>No, that is not there.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>The hon. member will find I am correct. These regulations were introduced in connection with sabotage. We had a very serious state of affairs in the country. The police knew well what people were involved in this sabotage. They knew where to find those people, but they knew that they would also involve other people in danger if they followed the usual course. In the meanwhile dynamite was used.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>But in this case there was nothing of that sort.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I am coming to that. The object of the regulations was to deal with the very difficult and serious situation in the country. The regulations related to sabotage, and they had to be strictly applied, and they were also absolutely effective. They complied with our requirements. Because we published those regulations at that time and carried them out we saved many people in the country from being the victims of violence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>We are not talking about that now. You are now setting up skittles in order to bowl them over.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No, I am not doing that. It was done because the war policy of the Government was at stake. We could not allow the war policy of the Government to be wrecked, and the enemies of the country and of the Government to be assisted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>But who complained about that?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>If the hon. member admits that it makes it easier <span class="col_8037-8038" refersTo="page_0320"/>for me to reply. Then I come to the question of diamonds. I want to say at once that the point has been rightly mentioned by the hon. member for Fauresmith, and I do not take exception to him having done so. I will also see that these regulations are not applied except where it is necessary. In this case they were applied because there was theft of diamonds.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Not theft, there was an infraction of the diamond law.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I shall give you information about that. We discovered that not only were diamonds being sold illegally on a large scale but that those diamonds were being sent out of the country. We found that the diamonds were going to North Africa, from where it would have been very easy to transfer them to enemy countries. We knew that the enemy was short of diamonds for industrial purposes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Was there any indication that these were industrial diamonds?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Yes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Where has there been any suggestion that these were industrial diamonds? No such suggestion has ever been made.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I admit that. When we discovered this matter, before we knew who the accused were we knew that diamonds were being smuggled to North Africa on a big scale, and from there they could easily get into the hands of Germany. We did not know whether they were industrial diamonds or not. We knew that diamonds had gone out and that they could get into the hands of the enemy, and to prevent that, and perfectly rightly, after thorough consideration we made this regulation applicable.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Was there any theft?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No, it was I.D.B.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>They were unlawfully in the possession of diamonds but it was not theft?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>They came into the possession of diamonds in a secret way in order to smuggle them to the North. We had a strong suspicion that the diamonds were being conveyed to Turkey, from where they could easily go to Germany.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>Did they go by air to North Africa?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>No, I do not want to talk about that. We could not know what sort of diamonds they were. The risk of industrial diamonds was there. What is more, it is not only industrial diamonds that can be used for industrial purposes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>How can the other diamonds be used for industrial purposes?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>It is true industrial diamonds are much cheaper, but the other diamonds can also be used for industrial purposes. If the hon. member had thought of that he would not have made this attack. We must take that into account.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>*Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>But were these diamonds conveyed to the North by American or British aircraft?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>We knew that the best way to stop it was to take action in our own country, and aucordingly we did so. If we had not taken those steps diamonds would have been exported on a large scale, and those diamonds would eventually have gone to Germany, where they were highly necessary for war purposes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swart">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWART</person>:</from>

<p>But tell us what subversive organisation there was to export the diamonds.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Tell Us whether one of those diamonds was discovered beyond the borders of the Union.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Yes.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>Where?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Many of these diamonds were never recovered by us.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#d&#x00F6;nges">

<from>*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D&#x00D6;NGES</person>:</from>

<p>But did you get them beyond the borders of the Union?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>*The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>Those that we did get were in this country, but the fact is that we found people in the country with great quantities of diamonds in their possession, and I believe it is certain if we had not taken those steps industrial diamonds would have been exported on a big scale, and they would eventually have found their way to Germany I said that the hon. member for Fauresmith apparently did not know this or otherwise he would not have mentioned this matter. No one is more keen to maintain the law of the land than this Government. But we must take into consideration that we are dealing with a period of martial law. In a time of war strong action has to be taken in such matters. I say that in comparison with martial law, and in com <span class="col_8039-8040" refersTo="page_0321"/>parison with what has been done in other countries where martial law prevails, the Government of the Union has acted leniently. I think we all should accept that a Government has no right to deal gently with people who assist the enemy and especially with people who help the enemy to make ammunition and to kill our own lads with it.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#swanepoel">

<from>&#x2020;*Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">SWANEPOEL</person>:</from>

<p>When a little while ago I mentioned communistic agitation amongst the natives the Minister of Justice stated that they were German agents or Nazis who were engaged in this agitation and that he had either put them in gaol or interned them. The Minister also issued a challenge, stating that we on this side could mention not a single instance where a person was guilty of agitation of this character amongst the natives. Last year I brought to the attention of the Minister in this House that Senator Basner was personally one of the causes of the rebellion of the natives in the Pietersburg district. The Minister is aware that this is the case. At that time the Minister made no reply. Subsequently I mentioned the matter for the second time, and again the Minister ran away and gave no reply.
